questions.question:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. All birds are cats.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: C inside D inside B: all cats are birds follows; all birds are cats does not.

questions.question:
Statements: Some pens are books. All books are tables.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are tables. II. All tables are books.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The pens that are books are inside tables. Not all tables need be books.

questions.question:
Statements: No flower is a tree. All trees are plants.
Conclusions: I. No flower is a plant. II. Some plants are not flowers.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Trees are plants and are not flowers, so some plants are not flowers. Flowers may still be plants, so I does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: Some A are B.
Conclusions: I. Some B are A. II. All A are B.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: "Some" statements convert. II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B.
Conclusions: I. Some A are B. II. Some B are A.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A is inside B, so some A are B and some B are A.

questions.question:
Statements: No A is B.
Conclusions: I. No B is A. II. All A are B.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The No statement converts. II contradicts the statement.

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B. Some B are C.
Conclusions: I. Some A are C. II. Some C are B.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: II is the converse of "Some B are C". I does not follow because the overlap with C may be outside A.

questions.question:
Statements: Some A are B. Some B are C.
Conclusions: I. Some A are C. II. Some C are A.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Two particular statements give no conclusion about A and C.

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B. No B is C.
Conclusions: I. No A is C. II. Some A are C.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A is inside B and B is separate from C, so no A is C. II contradicts it.

questions.question:
Statements: No A is B. No B is C.
Conclusions: I. No A is C. II. All A are C.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Two negative statements give no conclusion; I and II are both uncertain.

questions.question:
Statements: Some A are B. All B are C.
Conclusions: I. Some A are C. II. Some C are B.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The overlap of A and B lies inside C, and B is inside C, so some C are B.

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B. Some A are C.
Conclusions: I. Some B are C. II. All C are B.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The part of A that is C is also in B, so some B are C. C may extend outside B.

questions.question:
Statements: Some A are not B. All B are C.
Conclusions: I. Some A are not C. II. No A is C.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The A that is not B may still be in C. Neither follows.

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B. All C are B.
Conclusions: I. All A are C. II. Some C are A.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A and C are both inside B but may not touch.

questions.question:
Statement: All A are B.
Conclusions: I. Some B are not A. II. All B are A.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: If A is smaller than B, I is true. If A = B, II is true. One of them is always true, so either I or II follows.

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B. All B are C. Some C are D.
Conclusions: I. Some A are D. II. Some D are C. III. All A are C.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: A inside B inside C gives III. II is the converse of the third statement. I does not follow because the D overlap may be outside A.

questions.question:
Statements: No A is B. Some B are C. All C are D.
Conclusions: I. Some C are not A. II. Some D are not A.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Some B are C, and those C are not A (no A is B), so I. They are also D, so some D are not A.

questions.question:
Statements: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are singers. No singer is a dancer.
Conclusions: I. Some doctors are singers. II. No teacher is a dancer. III. Some doctors are not dancers.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Doctors who are teachers are singers (I). Teachers are singers, who are not dancers (II). Those doctors are not dancers (III).

questions.question:
Statements: All A are B. No B is C. Some D are C.
Conclusions: I. Some D are not B. II. Some D are not A. III. Some B are D.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The D that are C are not B (no B is C), so I. Those D are also not A (all A are B), so II. III need not hold.

questions.question:
Statements: Some A are B. No B is C.
Conclusions: I. Some A are not C. II. No A is C. III. Some B are not A.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The A that are B cannot be C, so some A are not C. II and III need not hold.
